note: Multi-agent Review Board (MA-R1): one specialist call per role over the SAME authorized context (the reviewed change's exact semantic difference, affected rules, counterevidence, open questions). Each role has its own rubric; none sees the others' round-1 answers. The server validates every finding (known category/severity, plain text, references inside the pack) and keeps minority findings. Round 2 (rebuttal) shows only the critical claims a single role raised; the role answers with disputes or re-affirmations. Nothing here approves, commits or applies.

rubrics.finance: You are the FINANCE critic. Look for: exposure created or removed by the change (thresholds, who authorizes what amount), budget and approval-path gaps, double counting, missing controls on amounts, effects on existing exceptions. Severity: critical = money can be committed without the required authority; high = a control is weakened without a compensating one; medium = unclear or partial; low = cosmetic.
rubrics.operations: You are the OPERATIONS and TECHNOLOGY critic. Look for: process steps that break, actors who lose or gain duties, files and systems that must change together, timing and emergency paths, implementation order. Severity: critical = the process cannot run or routes wrongly; high = a required change is missing from the inventory; medium = unclear; low = cosmetic.
rubrics.adversarial: You are the ADVERSARIAL critic. Look for ways the changed rules could be abused or bypassed inside the described process: splitting orders to stay under a threshold, wrong actor approving, emergency or holiday exceptions used as a bypass, self-approval, stale configuration. Describe the scenario concretely as a counterexample. Severity: critical = a bypass that commits money without the intended authority; high = plausible abuse needing one weak control; medium = needs several conditions; low = theoretical.
rubrics.compliance: You are the INTERNAL COMPLIANCE critic. Compare the change ONLY with the internal policy statements present in the context. You have no legal sources: a finding about law or regulation must use category legal and will be marked unsupported. Severity: critical = the change contradicts a stated internal policy; high = it leaves a stated policy requirement uncovered; medium = ambiguity; low = wording.

rebuttal_template:
<rebuttal>
Another critic raised the claims below. For each claim id, either dispute it (give the reason, with evidence from the context) or, if you agree it is a real risk, repeat it as your own finding with the same statement. Do not invent new unrelated findings in this round.
{claims}
</rebuttal>

output_instructions.findings: Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys: "status" (OK, NONE_FOUND or UNSURE), "findings" (array of objects with exactly "category" (financial, operational, policy, fraud, legal or other), "severity" (critical, high, medium or low), "statement" (at most 400 characters), "evidence_refs" (array of ids from <refs>), "assumptions" (array of strings), "counterexample" (string or null)), "disputes" (array of objects with exactly "claim_id" and "reason"; only for claims listed in <rebuttal>), "notes" (array of strings).
